text:
Sam K: quick sync on sampling controls + timepicker UX for latency dashboards. Current problem: when users select 1h with sampling=auto we downsample aggressively and p95 spikes are smoothed out. Folks confuse that with 'platform hiding spikes'. We need clearer affordances.

Riya S: yep seen this in support. Two quick proposals: show a small badge on the card 'sampled' with a tooltip explaining sampling level and effective resolution; OR add an explicit 'preserve peaks' toggle that disables downsampling for exact percentiles.

Ben J: +1 on the badge. I worry about extra toggles—will confuse non-power users. Could we surface a 2-state control: 'High fidelity' vs 'Auto (recommended)' with microcopy explaining cost/latency tradeoff?

Ana M: copy draft: 'Auto (recommended) — balances precision and performance. Switch to High fidelity to preserve transient spikes; may increase query cost.' Short and scannable.

Sam K: nice. For visuals: the badge should sit top-right of the p95 card (small pill). Tooltip should show current downsample ratio, e.g., 'Sampling: 1 of 10 points retained (resolution: 30s)'. Also show an inline example sparkline with markers for dropped buckets when you open the tooltip.

Riya S: accessibility notes: badge must be keyboard focusable and have aria-haspopup="true" if it opens the tooltip panel. Tooltip content should be readable by screen readers; better to open a small dialog on keyboard to avoid ephemeral tooltips.

Ben J: regarding p95 calculation: we should annotate when the percentile is computed on downsampled data vs full resolution. Maybe append an asterisk next to value with aria-description: 'computed on sampled data' and hover text that explains how much variance sampling can introduce.

Ana M: also UX for timepicker presets: current presets (15m, 1h, 6h) are fine but we could add 'Last greppable window' like 'Last 5m of traffic' for tailing sessions. Suggest adding 'Tail live' state that pins to the newest data and shows a clear live badge; when tailing is on, sampling should default to lower downsampling to show spikes.

Sam K: implementation questions: do we want sampling to be global per-dashboard or per-card? Per-card gives control but more UI surface. Support case shows users want to compare p95 across services with same fidelity — maybe global default with overrides per-card.

Riya S: agree: global setting in the toolbar, per-card override in card overflow menu. Default is 'Auto (recommended)'. We'll include a 'Reset to dashboard default' action on overrides.

Ben J: performance note: disabling downsampling will increase the query payload. Backend can cap points returned and show 'truncated' notice. Also add server-side flag in the response: sampling.level and sampling.method so frontend can present accurate microcopy.

Ana M: design tasks: 1) mock badge + tooltip (keyboard dialog variant) 2) microcopy for modes + asterisk copy 3) per-card menu mock for override 4) toolbar global control mock. I'll update the figma and tag Sam/Riya: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz123/latency-dashboard-sampling  (draft frames 3-6).

Sam K: dev tasks: add UI token for sampled badge, ARIA dialog for keyboard, wire up per-card override in settings API, and render sampling metadata from backend. Create ticket in GH with acceptance criteria.

Riya S: acceptance criteria in ticket please: - badge visible when sampling != full resolution - keyboard accessible dialog with explanation - asterisk shown for computed values + SR text - global control + per-card override - backend sampling metadata present and surfaced - e2e test that toggles high fidelity and verifies p95 changes (non-flaky)

Ben J: PR placeholder: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4999 (WIP) — I'll push backend bits after design signoff.

Ana M: will post updated frames and copy in figma comments. Sam/Riya can we do a quick 15-min sync tomorrow after you look?

Sam K: yes Tuesday 11a works for me. Thanks! :calendar:
